subject.title: [Feature]: Support to edit system prompt template

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class user-editable override contract for OpenClaw-owned system prompt sections such as Safety, Tool Call Style, OpenClaw Control, and Self-Update?
rationale: The request changes model-facing safety guidance, prompt precedence, and public customization trust boundaries, while current code intentionally exposes only narrower provider, hook, bootstrap, channel, and SDK prompt surfaces.

options.title: Approve Scoped Section Overrides
options.body: Add a narrow named-section override model with explicit edit authority, precedence, security docs, prompt-cache behavior, and regression tests.

options.title: Reject Core Section Overrides
options.body: Keep OpenClaw-owned sections fixed and document provider overlays, channel prompts, plugin hooks, and bootstrap files as the supported customization paths.

options.title: Defer To Narrower Prompt Work
options.body: Let identity-line, config-rules, and hook-replacement work proceed independently while leaving broad Safety/template editing unresolved here.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped Section Overrides
recommendation.body: Add a narrow named-section override model with explicit edit authority, precedence, security docs, prompt-cache behavior, and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest recent history on the provider-owned prompt contribution boundary and prior review context for this product/security decision.
